episodes.169591: An approaching cold front was aided by rather strong mid-level flow (45-55+ kts) and moderately strong MLCAPE (1000-2000 J/kg) over central Pennsylvania during the afternoon of July 12, 2022. Scattered showers and storms developed by early afternoon, and produced reports of wind damage and quarter-sized hail. Storms had exited the Lower Susquehanna Valley by early evening.
episodes.169596: As a backdoor cold front moved into eastern New Mexico, it replinished moisture and provided favorable upslope to allow for more rigorous thunderstorms on July 11, 2022. Thunderstorms developed early in the day and became widespread across much of the northern and central New Mexico. Heavy rainfall was common with these thunderstorms, especially across the northeast due to the boundary. Flash flooding once again impacted the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar. Flash flooding also impacted Highway 56 near Springer. Meanwhile, a few of these thunderstorms became severe with strong winds measured in both Clayton and Fort Sumner.
episodes.169600: As above normal moisture remained in place across northern and central New Mexico, a very active monsoon pattern persisted with numerous thunderstorms impacting the area on July 12, 2022. The Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar continued to be a magnet for heavy rainfall as an estimated 1.5 inches of rain resulted in flooding of roadways near Chacon.
episodes.169629: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms dropped south from middle Tennessee into north Alabama.  Strong winds associated knocked down a few trees.  Power outages (up to 20,000 people affected) were reported over a large part of central and northwest Madison County.  At least one foot of flood water was reported on one northern Madison County roadway.
episodes.169649: A mid-level disturbance moved into a marginally unstable airmass across southeast Ontario Canada and northern NY during the afternoon of July 12th. Scattered thunderstorms developed across Ontario and moved into northern New York with a few producing damaging winds.
episodes.169662: A strong mid-level disturbance moved into a moderately unstable airmass across VT during the afternoon of July 12th. Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the state with scattered damage in southern-eastern VT and some isolated damage near the Canadian border. Some more organized wind damage occurred in the communities of Chester, Wood stock-Hartford and White River Junction.
episodes.169750: A cold front triggered a few late evening severe thunderstorms between the I-69 and M-59 corridors. Damaging winds and a weak tornado near Lake Fenton occurred.
episodes.169766: A line of strong thunderstorms moved south across Lake Michigan on the evening of July 11.
episodes.169888: An upper level short wave trough moving through northern New England combined with an advancing cold front to produce severe thunderstorms in the late afternoon and evening hours.  Despite low K Indices and dry air aloft, the storms managed to strengthen and the dry air helped enhance the severe wind gusts.  The storms mainly impacted areas from western MA east-southeastward into northern CT and northern RI.
episodes.169889: An upper level short wave trough moving through northern New England combined with an advancing cold front to produce severe thunderstorms in the late afternoon and evening hours.  Despite low K Indices and dry air aloft, the storms managed to strengthen and the dry air helped enhance the severe wind gusts.  The storms mainly impacted areas from western MA east-southeastward into northern CT and northern RI.
episodes.170121: During the afternoon and evening of Tuesday, July 12th, a weak cold front was moving southward across central Minnesota. A cluster of storms developed ahead of this front, and with 30-40 knots of effective wind shear, a few severe wind gusts occurred across central and east central Minnesota. Although instability was weak, there was enough DCAPE with the strongest storms to produce these damaging winds.
episodes.170609: An outbreak of significant severe weather occurred during the afternoon and evening hours of Tuesday, July 12th, 2022. An unseasonably strong cold front interacted with a high instability airmass to result in several bowing lines of thunderstorms, which maintained their organization and intensity due to strong atmospheric wind shear. Swaths of widespread damaging winds were observed, much of which was considerable. A couple of tornadoes were also confirmed, along with some significant hail. A wind gust of over 100 MPH was measured in one of the most powerful storms over eastern West Virginia.

episodes.170972: Thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the early evening hours on Tuesday (7/12).  The strongest storm produced a wind gust to 62 mph in Brown County.
episodes.171050: A frontal boundary swung into the Central Appalachians on July 12th and interrupted quiet weather provided by high pressure the day prior. Initially, showers and storms evolved along the front across Ohio and then spread eastward into West Virginia that afternoon and evening. Strong winds, large hail, and heavy downpours encompassed these showers and storms, leading to instances of tree damage and high water issues across the state.
episodes.171074: Isolated thunderstorms developed leading to some significant wind damage in Delmarva. Most notably was a macroburst which began near Denton, MD and continued for about 18 miles east into Delaware with estimated peak winds of 110 mph.
episodes.171075: An upper-level trough brought along a cold front as it passed through Northeastern Pennsylvania. This system brought scattered thunderstorms to the region. One storm became severe with damaging winds and knocked down a couple of trees in Luzerne County.
episodes.171076: An upper-level trough brought along a cold front as it passed through Central New York. This system brough many thunderstorms to the region. Damaging wind gusts were the main hazard and some minor damage to personal property occurred.
episodes.171077: Isolated thunderstorms developed leading to some significant wind damage in Delmarva. A macroburst began near Denton, MD and continued for about 18 miles east into Delaware with estimated peak winds of 110 mph. Two other microbursts occurred as well, one near Middletown and one near Seaford.
episodes.171078: A discrete supercell developed in Carbon County passing toward the Delaware Water Gap which lead to some scattered wind damage.
episodes.171079: A discrete supercell tracked from near the Delaware Water Gap toward New York City along I-80 producing scattered wind damage along its path. Another discrete severe thunderstorm passed eastward out of New Castle County, DE and produced scattered wind damage in Salem and Cumberland Counties.
episodes.171316: An upper level disturbance crossed the region during the afternoon and evening of the 12th in advance of an approaching cold front. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and persisted into the evening. Some of the thunderstorms reached severe levels producing damaging winds.
episodes.171368: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a trough of low pressure in a very hot airmass. One of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171411: A couple of isolated severe storms produced localized wind damage in the form of a few downed trees, tree limbs and power lines.
episodes.171616: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced quarter sized hail in western Laramie County during the mid afternoon hours on July 12th.
episodes.171701: A cluster of thunderstorms developed along the southeast Georgia coast and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.171702: Isolated thunderstorms developed along the Charleston County coast in the late afternoon hours. One thunderstorms produced a lightning strike to a residence and produced damage.
episodes.171898: A broad upper level high centered near the 4-Corners region extended to the east coast north of Florida. The eastern portion of the ridge rapidly eroded as an upper level trough dove south across the Great Lakes to the Ohio River Valley. Locally, there was some form of residual frontal boundary draped across the area. The morning local upper air sounding showed ample instability for robust thunderstorm development as well as ample moisture available. That combo along with a boundary for storms to focus on provided the environment for a thunderstorm to produce flash flooding over portions of St. Tammany Parish.
episodes.171952: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front resulted in widespread wind damage across eastern New York during the afternoon and evening hours on Tuesday July 12, 2022. A NWS Storm Survey concluded that a microburst touched down near Fort Miller in Washington County that resulted in an injury.
episodes.171965: Several rounds of severe weather occurred during the July 9-13 time frame. These rounds of thunderstorms were the result of two cold fronts moving across the state in association with a surface low moving along the boundary.
episodes.171969: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front resulted in multiple wind damage reports across southern Vermont during the afternoon and evening hours on Tuesday July 12, 2022.
episodes.171973: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front resulted in multiple wind damage reports across western Massachusetts during the afternoon and evening hours on Tuesday July 12, 2022. A NWS Storm Survey concluded an area of straight line wind damage with estimated wind speeds of 85 mph occurred across the Town of Lenox. There was one fatality reported just south of Lenox (Berkshire County) due to a large tree falling onto a pickup truck.
episodes.171974: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front resulted in a couple of wind damage reports across northwest Connecticut during the afternoon and evening hours of Tuesday July 12, 2022.
episodes.172145: Thunderstorms formed ahead of a cold front which crossed the Upper Ohio Valley on July 12th.  Most storms formed near and south of the Mason-Dixon Line into WV, as moisture was too limited further north. Sufficient instability and shear were realized for several wind damage reports.
episodes.172211: Strong to severe thunderstorms occurred over and near the higher terrain on this day, along with parts of the southern I-25 corridor. Large hail was the main hazard observed, with the largest hail of 1.75 inches observed near Trinidad.
episodes.172272: A few strong storms developed ahead of a cold front over northeastern Minnesota during the afternoon of the 12th. Storms remained under severe limits but one storm did produce nickel-sized hail near Cook.
episodes.172361: High pressure ridge axis across south FL lifted a weak warm front along the Altamaha river northward. Moist southwest flow and slightly faster storm motion led to storms developing off the Gulf of mexico into the suwannee valley in the morning and then pushed northeastward in the early afternoon with more numerous storms progressing through inland southeast Georgia towards the Georgia coast and also along portions of the northeast Florida coast along the pinned Atlantic seabreeze. Stronger storms developed along the sea breeze merger along the I-95 corridor producing street flooding, penny size hail and a funnel cloud.
episodes.172362: High pressure ridge axis across south FL lifted a weak warm front along the Altamaha river northward. Moist southwest flow and slightly faster storm motion led to storms developing off the Gulf of mexico into the suwannee valley in the morning and then pushed northeastward in the early afternoon with more numerous storms progressing through inland southeast Georgia towards the Georgia coast and also along portions of the northeast Florida coast along the pinned Atlantic seabreeze. Stronger storms developed along the sea breeze merger along the I-95 corridor producing street flooding, penny size hail and a funnel cloud.
episodes.172365: Showers and thunderstorms developed along a cold front which pushed through Kentucky during the afternoon and evening hours on July 12th. Immediately ahead of the front, temperatures in the upper 80s and lower 90s combined with dewpoints in the mid-70s to facilitate the development of greater than 3000 J/kg mixed-layer CAPE. With plenty of fuel to work with, storms grew rapidly, especially across south central Kentucky, leading to isolated wind damage reports in association with the strongest cells.||On July 14th, the mid-level trough which brought the cold front and associated thunderstorms through Kentucky two days prior began to shift off to the east. A weak surface frontal boundary developed over portions of southwestern Kentucky, and frontal convergence along with modest instability helped contribute to the development of scattered strong thunderstorms across southern and central Kentucky. One of these storms was just strong enough to produce scattered wind damage across Grayson County.
episodes.172372: Isolated afternoon thunderstorms developed across much of west central Texas. A few storms were severe and produced wind damage. On July 12th, a significant microburst was reported in Tom Green County, 6 miles east of Arden.
episodes.172495: A combination of weak steering flow and tropical moisture resulted in slow moving thunderstorms with torrential downpours that produced a few instances of flash flooding.
episodes.172505: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots as well as a few sightings of waterspouts.
episodes.172556: A large thunderstorm complex tracked southeast from Kentucky and Middle Tennessee into East Tennessee during the late afternoon and evening hours. Wind damage was reported across the northern Cumberland Plateau and the central Tennessee Valley. Flash flooding near Pittman Center and in the Greenbriar area of the National Park.
episodes.172588: Surface heating ahead of an eastward advancing front resulted in ample instability, and when coupled with modest shear, lead to multiple afternoon thunderstorms across Southeast West Virginia. Several of these storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.172589: Surface heating ahead of an eastward advancing front resulted in ample instability, and when coupled with modest shear, lead to multiple afternoon thunderstorms across southwest Virginia.
episodes.172648: A cold front approached eastern Kentucky during the day on Tuesday July 12. It then slowed and eventually stalled across eastern Kentucky during the afternoon and evening hours. With most of the area seeing plenty of time for heating and destabalization ahead of the front, the presence of the boundary across the region was the added lift needed to spawn strong thunderstorms that resulted in multiple instances of wind damage, mainly across McCreary and Bell Counties. Pulaski County also experienced some localized damage.
episodes.172676: Scattered thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. One storm produced a severe wind gust in Sierra Vista.
episodes.172719: An area of low pressure tracked to the north of the region across Quebec province, with a trailing cold front pushing westward across New England during the afternoon hours of July 12th.  A hot and unstable airmass was in place across New Hampshire with above normal temperatures.  A pre-frontal trough axis ahead of the surface boundary was the focus area of thunderstorm development.  A broken line of Severe Thunderstorms developed bringing damaging wind and hail from the Connecticut River Valley across the state to the Maine state border.
episodes.172720: An area of low pressure tracked to the north of the region across Quebec province, with a trailing cold front pushing westward across New England during the afternoon hours of July 12th. A hot and unstable airmass was in place across southwest Maine, with above normal temperatures. A pre-frontal trough axis ahead of the surface boundary was the focus area of thunderstorm development. A broken line of Severe Thunderstorms developed in New Hampshire and moved eastward towards Maine.  Most storms began to weaken on the line but a storm traveling through the Lakes Region remained severe.
episodes.172721: An area of low pressure tracked to the north of the region across Quebec province, with a trailing cold front pushing westward across New England during the afternoon hours of July 12th. A broken line of Severe Thunderstorms developed in New Hampshire and moved eastward towards Maine. episodes.172950: A moist south to southwest wind flow led to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours over the interior of South Florida and Lake Okeechobee.
episodes.172968: Waterspouts developed in association with a convective cloud line that formed within weak southwest to west lower tropospheric flow.
episodes.172986: The largest severe weather event of summer 2022 affected much of Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on July 12, with numerous severe thunderstorms producing large hail and wind damage. Up to softball size hail was reported in the Chapel Hill area of Marshall County, which is the largest hail reported in Middle Tennessee in many years.

An NWS storm survey confirmed a weak tornado developed over or along the shoreline of eastern Lake Fenton during the late evening of July 11th. The tornado tracked east-southeast for 7.5 miles before lifting 3 miles east-southeast of Holly/just west of I-75 in northern Oakland County. The first indication of damage occurred on Pine Street near Lake Fenton where large limbs fell on a home, which took out a second-story dormer and a portion of the roof. Tree damage was sparse and sporadic along the path, mainly consisting of tree limbs and leaves down. The weak tornado crossed into northwest Oakland County just southwest of Oyster Lake, and continued tracking southeast for an additional 6.1 miles. The peak damage was observed in the backyard of a home on Addis Road in Holly. About a dozen trees suffered significant damage. The home also lost a few vinyl siding panels and a pergola was damaged. A barn farther down the road lost some metal roofing.

A powerful storm tracked across southern Hampshire County on July 12th, 2022, producing a 23-mile long by 9-mile wide swath of extensive tree and property damage. The vast majority of this damage was associated with a macroburst as a bowing storm and associated rear-inflow jet tracked across the county. Winds within this 9-mile wide swath were estimated to be between 60 and 105 MPH.||Within Hampshire County, sporadic tree damage was noted as far west as Purgitsville, but more appreciable damage began in the vicinity of the South Branch of the Potomac River several miles to the south of Romney, West Virginia. Significant tree damage associated with the bowing portion of the storm extended south of Arnold Farm Lane along CR-8 South Branch River Road and CR-6 Trough Road for about four miles. Within this stretch of damage, entire corn fields were leveled just to the south of Trough View Road. Dozens of trees were blown down in this area, as well. Wind gusts were estimated to be as high as 70 MPH in this section of the county.

A powerful storm tracked across southern Hampshire County on July 12th, 2022, producing a 23-mile long by 9-mile wide swath of extensive tree and property damage. The vast majority of this damage was associated with a macroburst as a bowing storm and associated rear-inflow jet tracked across the county. Winds within this 9-mile wide swath were estimated to be between 60 and 105 MPH.||The storm progressed into the valley between Nathaniel Mountain and Short Mountain between about 3:43 and 3:53 PM EDT. Extensive tree damage was observed throughout this valley over a several mile long swath extending from north to south. The most extensive damage was observed just north of Kirby. Hundreds of trees were either snapped or uprooted, and a high level of defoliation was observed on any trees that remained due to wind-driven hail. Two-inch diameter hail was observed near Kirby, and accumulating golf ball size hail was observed near Hampshire Gas Company off of Grass Lick Road. Significant hail damage occurred at Hampshire Gas Company. A personal weather station measured a wind gust of 89 knots (102 MPH) just to the north of Hampshire Gas Company, while a weather station on site at Hampshire Gas Company failed in the wind-driven hail. The maximum level of defoliation was noted in the vicinity of where the 102 MPH gust was recorded and where the accumulating golf ball size hail was observed. Most of this area likely observed winds of 75 to 90 MPH, with winds in excess of 100 MPH being localized to near the sensor immediately in the lee of Nathaniel Mountain.

Within the valley east of Short Mountain, sporadic tree damage was noted as far north as around 4 miles north of Delray, but much more extensive tree damage was observed from Delray southward to Rio (a 5-mile wide swath). A powerful storm tracked across southern Hampshire County on July 12th, 2022, producing a 23-mile long by 9-mile wide swath of extensive tree and property damage. The vast majority of this damage was associated with a macroburst as a bowing storm and associated rear-inflow jet tracked across the county. Winds within this 9-mile wide swath were estimated to be between 60 and 105 MPH.||The storm progressed out of the North River Valley and crossed another range of mountains before progressing into the Cacapon River Valley.
